# Prospect shortlist — bakeries & patisseries worth calling (Europe + North America)

Compiled 2026-10-10 from public award lists, regional “best bakery” round-ups and competition coverage.
**36 prospects · 83,545 € one-off pipeline · 97,585 € first-year value (care included) · 1,170 €/month recurring if all close.**
Machine-readable: `sales/prospects-2026.csv` (19 + 5 verification columns) — also on Drive as a Sheet.

## Verification is part of the job — and it already changed the list

I checked **5 leads** properly today (search + opening their actual pages). Result: my own
article-sourced notes were wrong in three cases, which changes both the pitch and the price.

| Lead | Reality found 2026-10-10 | What we now say |
|---|---|---|
| **Forn Pa Serra** (BCN) | No site, no socials — confirmed. Their name is represented by a scraper page `pa-serra.weeblyte.com` **with wrong opening hours**. Phone +34 934 242 541. | “People read the wrong hours online and stay away. One page, three languages, correct hours, WhatsApp reservation.” |
| **Handy Bakery** (Gràcia, BCN) | Opened ~Aug 2025, El Periódico feature. Own domain `handybakery.es` = **one sentence: “Contáctanos por Instagram”**. Wholesale dropped 70 % → 50 %, so retail conversion is the pain. Address is *Carrer de Rabassa 5* (my earlier note had the wrong street). | “You have the press and the room; the domain is empty. Menu + hours + pre-order turns walk-bys into orders.” |
| **August Bakery** (London) | Has a Squarespace site with a contact form — *not* Instagram-only as I first wrote. No menu, no prices, one language. hello@august-bakery.com · +44 7707 038794. | “Keep Squarespace. Bolt on a bilingual menu + pre-order page we host and link from your nav.” |
| **Northern Rye** (Newcastle) | Has `northern-rye.co.uk`, shop@northern-rye.co.uk, **two locations + new larger bakehouse since 2024** — so the gap is wholesale ordering, not design. Quote re-rated €1,017 → **€2,385** (Croissant + wholesale + multi-location). | “Trade-counter ordering + per-location hours + a notify-me on the country sourdough.” |
| **Weltons Tiny Bakeshop** (Charleston) | Own domain exists; **no public email** → phone/contact form only. +1 843-666-7277. | Call at 13:30 (after the queue, before the close). A James Beard finalist with no way to reserve is the whole pitch. |

Three lessons for the remaining 31: *aggregator articles are a lead source, not evidence*; the pitch is
always “what is verifiably missing”, never “your site is bad”; and a wrong address in your own CRM is how
you lose a lead before you even write.

| Segment | Count | One-off |
|---|---|---|
| A — hot (no usable presence, or a press moment now) | 7 | 16,715 € |
| B — upgrade (site exists, missing ordering/languages) | 29 | 66,830 € |

By country: US 27,186 €, GB 25,670 €, FR 15,455 €, ES 15,234 €.

## Before anyone is contacted

1. Do the 4-minute check (Google the name+city, open the IG bio, open the Google Business profile, WHOIS
   the domain if one is claimed) and fill `verified_2026-10-10` + `contact_verified` in the CSV.
2. Read `sales/COMPLIANCE.md`. Short version: B2B cold email is legal in FR/UK/US **with** your real
   identity, a source line, and a free way to object — and never through a marketing platform's opt-in
   list rules.
3. One personalised message per shop, 5–10 a day max, from a mailbox with SPF/DKIM/DMARC.
4. Nothing goes out that you have not read. Especially not a price.

## Dial order

**Now, while it's fresh:** Forn Pa Serra (phone, no email exists), Handy Bakery (DM then call, they answer
Instagram), Boulangerie-Pâtisserie Familha (national M6 winner, village, zero funnel), Wild Crumb and
JinJu Patisserie (award + relocation/rebrand timing), August Bakery and Northern Rye (email verified —
drafts already prepared in Gmail).

**Second wave:** the B rows where a verifiable gap exists (no ordering, single language, wrong hours on
Google Business) — that is 29 of 36, and it is an *upgrade* pitch, not a rebuild pitch, which closes faster
at a lower price.

**Do not send:** anyone whose only “signal” is a two-year-old list, and any lead whose address came from a
personal Instagram DM — sole traders are closer to the B2C rule, so call or visit them instead.
